cards.title: What is the passive?
cards.body: In the active, the subject does the action. In the passive, the subject receives the action — the thing or person that is affected becomes the subject.
cards.body_cz: V činném rodě podmět děj dělá. V trpném podmět děj přijímá — věc nebo osoba, které se něco stane, je podmět.
points: Active: subject = doer (agent)
Passive: subject = receiver / thing affected

cards.title: When and why we use it
cards.body: Use the passive when the doer is **unknown**, **obvious**, **unimportant**, or you want the **result** first (news, signs, processes).
cards.body_cz: Passive používáme, když činitele **neznáme**, je **jasný**, **není důležitý**, nebo chceme na začátek dát **výsledek**.
points: **Unknown** doer: My bike was **stolen**. (We don’t know who.)
**Obvious** / general: English **is spoken** here.
**Process**: These phones **are made** in Asia.
**Result** first: The documents **were signed** yesterday.
Skip the doer when it would only be *someone / they / people*

cards.title: Form
cards.body: Passive = a form of **be** + past participle. Present and past are enough for this level’s basics.
cards.body_cz: Passive = **be** + příčestí. Pro základy stačí přítomný a minulý čas.

table.caption: Present / past passive
rows: These phones are made in Asia.

points: past participle = built, spoken, made, signed, grown…
Not now: has been done · is being built · must be finished (later)

cards.title: by + agent (optional)
cards.body: Add by + person/thing only when the doer matters. Most passives have no by-phrase.
cards.body_cz: by + kdo/co jen když je činitel důležitý. Většina trpných vět by nemá.
points: The film was directed by her. (agent useful)
English is spoken here. (no by — general)
If you always add by someone, you often don’t need the passive

cards.title: Czech comparison
cards.body: Czech often uses se / -no/-to / or a different word order where English prefers be + past participle. Don’t translate word-for-word — match the idea (thing affected first).
cards.body_cz: Čeština často se / -no/-to / jiný slovosled tam, kde angličtina má be + 3. tvar. Nepřekládej slovo od slova — drž smysl (věc, které se to týká, je podmět).

table.caption: Rough pairs (idea, not 1:1)
rows: Ukradli mi kolo. / Kolo mi ukradli.
These phones are made in Asia.
Tyhle telefony se vyrábějí v Asii.

points: se often ≈ English passive (process / general)
byl/byla/bylo + příčestí ≈ was/were + past participle
Active Czech (ukradli mi…) can still be passive English when the bike is the topic

cards.title: Active ↔ passive (same idea)
cards.body: Object of the active becomes subject of the passive. Be takes the tense; main verb becomes past participle.
cards.body_cz: Předmět činné věty se stane podmětem trpné. Be nese čas; hlavní sloveso jde do 3. tvar.

rows: They make these phones in Asia.
These phones are made in Asia.

cards.title: What you practise here
cards.body: Type **be + past participle**: *was cancelled*, *are made*. The base verb is in brackets.
cards.body_cz: Piš **be + příčestí**: *was cancelled*, *are made*. Základ slovesa je v závorce.
points: 1) Find the tense cue (every… / yesterday / in 2015 / still…)
2) Match number: singular is/was · plural are/were
Is the office cleaned every night? → Is (not Was)
The house ____ built in 1990. → was
will/must + ____ → be

cards.title: Questions
cards.body: Be moves to the front: Is coffee grown in Brazil? Was the window fixed last week?
cards.body_cz: Be jde dopředu: Is coffee grown in Brazil? Was the window fixed last week?
